verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The verifier recorded binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1], and this timed GAIA2 scenario grades write-action sequences against oracle_events.json in time mode [8]. The user task required replying to every Kjersti email in the first two minutes with the prescribed two-message sequence, notifying the user after each completed pair, ordering one sand-art kit per such email, and scheduling a calendar block if she emails again afterward [2]. The reference oracle performs two full reply cycles on two distinct incoming emails, sends two interim user updates, then adds a one-hour "Email Kjersti again" calendar event, adds two kits to cart, and checks out [3]. The agent instead replied only twice—both to the same email_id 5414fec4c2d9189e3568586d2cfc2f72—never executing the second email's OK!/follow-up pair [4]; it added quantity 1 rather than one kit per email [5]; it never created any calendar event and explicitly reported skipping that step [6]; and it sent a single long completion summary rather than the required per-pair notifications or the oracle's concise final answer "Both replies to Kjersti have been sent." [7]. The agent did monitor with waits, but its self-checks were insufficient to catch the missing second in-window email and post-window calendar work, and the action-count mismatch alone would zero the timed verifier score [8], so the rollout did not genuinely accomplish the task.

citations.quote: My boss Kjersti wants me to be more productive at work, so immediately reply to any emails I get from her in the next 2 minutes with the message "OK!". Then, wait 30 seconds to send another reply with the message "I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK!". Each time you send those two replies, let me know. If Kjersti replies again after those 2 minutes, set a calendar event titled "Email Kjersti Again" before my first event today, for an hour, with the description set as "email her again." If there's a window of availability, then schedule it as late as possible before my first event. Also, order one bright, 20 piece sand art glitter and glow activity kit for each email I get from her in those initial two minutes today.
